metadata.description: An uninterruptible power supply — battery-backed conditioned power that carries a load through an input failure and reports the state a graceful shutdown decides on. A base class of its own (ADR-075, the base test of CLS-002): NUT and Redfish PowerEquipment abstract over every UPS topology — double-conversion, line-interactive, standby (IEC 62040-3) — and every element here is honorable by each; it is not a kind of Facility (a folder), and no API abstracts a UPS together with a PDU or a transfer switch, so it sits under no wider power base. Vendor-neutral by construction: what every UPS declares (identity, rating, battery, low-battery policy) and reports (status, charge, runtime, load, input voltage); the telemetry producer (NUT, a vendor SNMP card, a Redfish power shelf) is a provider, named on the instance and in adopts[], never in the type. The circuit it protects is a PowerFeed that is supplied_by it — hosts keep depending on the feed, so the shutdown walk is unchanged.

identity.description: Unit identity (SPEC-DESIGN-REQUIREMENTS §27) — the same shape every Hardware/Machine type carries.

serial_number.description: Unit serial (Redfish SerialNumber; NUT ups.serial / device.serial).

topology.description: UPS topology per IEC 62040-3 performance classification: double-conversion (VFI), line-interactive (VI), standby (VFD).

rated_capacity.description: Nameplate rating (NUT ups.power.nominal / ups.realpower.nominal; Redfish PowerSupply/PowerShelf ratings).

battery.description: The battery set — what wears and what gets replaced. Runtime and charge are outputs, not declared here.

chemistry.description: Battery chemistry (NUT battery.type carries the vendor string; this is the neutral class).

count.description: Number of battery modules/packs installed (NUT battery.packs).

installed_at.description: Date the current battery set was installed (NUT battery.date / battery.mfr.date) — replacement planning.

outlets.description: Number of output receptacles (NUT outlet.count; Redfish Outlet collection size).

low_battery_policy.description: When the unit MUST raise low-battery — by remaining charge and/or remaining runtime.

charge_percent.description: Raise low-battery at or below this charge, percent.

runtime_seconds.description: Raise low-battery at or below this estimated runtime, seconds.

management_interfaces.description: How the unit can be observed and controlled — the surfaces present, not which one a provider uses.

status.description: Observed unit status — online | on-battery | low-battery | overload | off (maps from NUT ups.status OL / OB / LB / OVER / OFF; the meta-schema keeps outputs to type + description, so the vocabulary is stated here and on PowerFeed identically). The value a graceful shutdown triggers on.

runtime_seconds.description: Estimated runtime remaining on battery, seconds (NUT battery.runtime). Absent when the unit does not report it.

load_percent.description: Output load as a percent of rating (NUT ups.load).

firmware.description: Unit firmware version (NUT ups.firmware; Redfish FirmwareVersion).

relationships.name: located_in
relationships.description: located_in — the rack/room the unit sits in. Optional; a UPS is a power source wherever it stands.

adopts.role: the topology vocabulary — double-conversion, line-interactive, standby — reference by name only (IEC text is copyrighted)
telemetry variable namespace the outputs map from (status, charge, runtime, load, voltages) and the low-battery thresholds (battery.charge.low / battery.runtime.low) — reference-only: NUT is GPL
identity and rating vocabulary (Manufacturer, Model, SerialNumber, FirmwareVersion, capacity ratings)

context.purpose: Models the battery-backed unit itself — what it is rated for, what wears, when it must signal low battery, and what it reports — so the feed it protects can be supplied_by a real entity instead of a feed_type string.
context.plain_description: A UPS as a thing you own, separate from the circuit it protects. You declare its make and model, its rating, its battery set and the point at which it must announce low battery; it reports whether it is online or on battery, how much charge and runtime remain, and how loaded it is. The daemon or card that produces those numbers (NUT, a vendor SNMP card, a Redfish power shelf) is the provider on the instance, not part of the type. The circuit the UPS feeds stays a PowerFeed, now supplied_by the UPS, so nothing about shutdown ordering changes.
use_when: You need the UPS behind a power feed to be an entity — its identity, rating, battery age and low-battery policy — rather than a feed_type string.
You need live UPS telemetry (status, charge, runtime, load) attributed to the unit that produced it, with the producer recorded as a provider.
not_for: The circuit that equipment draws from — PowerFeed; hosts depend_on feeds, not on UPSes.
A PDU, transfer switch, or power shelf — no API abstracts them together with a UPS as one deliverable (ADR-075, CLS-002).
works_with: PowerFeed — a feed is supplied_by the UPS that conditions it.
Workload — the NUT upsd (or equivalent) that observes the unit is a service on a host, named as the instance's provider.
Automation.Job — the graceful-shutdown job that the unit's status drives, via the feed.
